task.description: WF-02 Step 2c hard gate on REQ-038's implementation: Letflow.Definitions.rollback_definition_version/4 (new, lib/letflow/definitions.ex) and the widening of PromotionReviewStore.supersede_review/3's allowed_source_statuses to add :approved (lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_review_store.ex, an already-merged, previously gate-approved module). Determine APPLIES/NOT-APPLICABLE for INV-1..INV-8 against git diff main...HEAD and run the How-to-verify procedure for each APPLIES invariant.
acceptance_criteria: Scope test run explicitly, not assumed
Every invariant INV-1..INV-8 given an explicit APPLIES/NOT-APPLICABLE verdict with reasoning
Each APPLIES invariant's How-to-verify procedure actually run, not taken on the producer's word
Permission-guard ordering (AC5) traced directly in the code, not read off the design doc's claim
The promotion_review_store.ex widening's actual security implication assessed on its own terms, not just flagged-and-passed
Cardinality-branching supersede-lookup's fail-safe direction confirmed by reading supersede_matching_review/4 directly

result.summary:
Reviewed git diff main...HEAD for the two in-scope files. Scope test: APPLIES -- diff modifies queries against tenant-scoped tables (process_definitions, promotion_reviews), so this is a tenant-data path per the scope test's first bullet even though no HTTP route or migration is added. Independently re-ran `mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors` (exit 0, 57 files, no warnings) rather than trusting ELIXIR-DEV's handoff claim. Traced rollback_definition_version/4's control flow directly: TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 is a pure string transform (confirmed by reading lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex lines 102-115 -- regex match + Ecto.UUID.cast, zero I/O, not a 'row read'), and permission_checker.(actor_id, tenant_id) is evaluated in the public function itself, strictly before do_rollback/6 (and therefore before run_rollback_transaction/4's FOR UPDATE lock) is ever called -- a false result returns {:error, :forbidden} with no Repo call of any kind having occurred. AC5/INV-RB-1 confirmed by code, not by the design doc's own claim. Confirmed both injectable opts (permission_checker, event_appender) are Keyword.fetch!/2'd with no built-in default, raising KeyError if omitted -- identical, no-default stance to Promotion.promote_definition/3 (lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex lines 100-104, 133-139), and confirmed no wrapping try/rescue anywhere treats a permission_checker exception as :ok (the only try/rescue in the new code wraps run_rollback_transaction/4 inside do_rollback/6 and converts an exception to {:error, {:transaction_failed, exception}} -- an error, not success). No weaker default was quietly invented.

INV-1 (tenant data isolation) -- APPLIES, PASS. (a) Every new Repo call threads prefix: prefix through explicitly: run_rollback_transaction/4's Repo.all and both swap_active_pointer/3 Repo.update_all calls, and supersede_matching_review/4's Repo.all, plus the prefix: prefix opt passed into PromotionReviewStore.supersede_review/3 (which itself scopes its internal Repo.get/Repo.update_all by prefix, confirmed by reading promotion_review_store.ex's transition/6 at lines 360-374 and execute_update/3 at lines 393-408 -- unchanged by this diff except the allowed_source_statuses list). No query in the diff reaches process_definitions or promotion_reviews outside :prefix-scoping. (b) No migration in this diff -- no table newly created, N/A. (c) No new tenant_id is ever written by this diff -- both process_definitions writes touch only status/updated_at, and the promotion_reviews write (via supersede_review/3) touches only status/superseded_by/row_version; tenant_id is used only as a read-filter (where d.tenant_id == ^tenant_id / r.tenant_id == ^tenant_id), itself derived from opts[:prefix] via TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 -- never accepted as a separate caller-supplied argument (rollback_definition_version/4's signature has no tenant_id parameter at all, matching INV-RB-9). Cross-tenant blast radius: single_review (looked up by id inside supersede_matching_review/4) was itself fetched from a query already filtered to r.tenant_id == ^tenant_id AND prefix: prefix, and PromotionReviewStore.supersede_review/3's own Repo.get is re-scoped by the same prefix -- physical schema-per-tenant isolation plus the intra-schema tenant_id filter both apply, no path for one tenant's rollback call to touch another tenant's process_definitions or promotion_reviews rows.

INV-2/INV-3/INV-5 -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No HTTP/Plug route added (S4 not started, confirmed no web/api-layer file in the diff), no Lua/WASM scripting surface touched (S5 not started), no lookup-by-ID *endpoint* introduced (rollback_definition_version/4 is a context-module function called by a future orchestrator/route, not a handler itself) -- matches this diff's own design doc §1 scope table, which explicitly defers the HTTP route to S4.

INV-4 (secrets by reference only) -- NOT-APPLICABLE to this specific diff. Grepped both changed files for System.get_env / hardcoded-secret-shaped literals (password|secret|client_secret|token assignment patterns) -- no matches, and manually confirmed no config/env/token-resolving code was touched at all by this diff (the two injectable opts, permission_checker and event_appender, are behavior hooks, not secret material). INV-4 is 'live' as a standing invariant but this diff does not touch a secret-resolving path, so the correct per-diff verdict is NOT-APPLICABLE, not a forced PASS against nothing.

INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping) -- APPLIES, PASS by virtue of this handoff itself: this document states explicitly which of INV-1..INV-8 apply and how each was verified, per the meta-invariant's own definition of satisfaction.

INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) -- APPLIES, PASS. `grep -n Repo.query lib/letflow/definitions.ex` returns zero matches. Every new query in the diff is built via Ecto.Query (where/lock/select) with pin-operator bindings (^tenant_id, ^process_key, ^target_version, ^current_active.id, ^target_row.id) -- no raw SQL, no string concatenation or interpolation of tenant/user-controlled data anywhere in the diff.

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES, PASS with one item manually reasoned through beyond the grep heuristic. The literal grep pattern (^\s*{:ok, .*} = ) matches nothing new in this diff. Manually inspected the diff for other bare-match risk and found one: swap_active_pointer/3's `{1, [activated_row]} = Repo.update_all(...)` for the target-row activation. This is a bare match that would raise if the update affected zero rows, but it is not a realistic-input crash risk: target_row.id was locked FOR UPDATE in the same Repo.transaction/1 (run_rollback_transaction/4, same function call, same DB transaction) immediately before swap_active_pointer/3 runs, so no concurrent transaction can have deleted or already-modified that specific row out from under this update -- Postgres row-level locking guarantees the WHERE id = ^target_row.id update affects exactly 1 row. This is structurally identical to the already-shipped, already-REVIEWER-approved activate_draft/2 precedent in the same module (same file, confirmed present before this diff), which uses the identical 'lock then bare-match the guaranteed-1-row update' shape. This is the INV-8 text's own named exception ('immediately after a value the same function already validated') -- not a violation, but noted explicitly here because it required stepping past the literal grep pattern to confirm, as this session's own procedure requires (manual confirmation, not heuristic-only).

Promotion_review_store.ex widening (task item 4) -- reasoning holds up, no unintended edge case found. Confirmed directly in the source (not just the moduledoc's claim): allowed_source_statuses is a per-call-site hardcoded list, and supersede_review/3's guarded update (execute_update/3, unchanged by this diff) re-checks `p.status == ^row.status` from the SAME pre-read at UPDATE time -- so :superseded itself is still not in any function's allowed_source_statuses list anywhere in the file (confirmed: reject_review/3 [:pending_review], mark_review_applied/2 [:approved], mark_review_failed/2 [:approved], supersede_review/3 now [:applied, :approved, :failed, :rejected]) -- a row already :superseded still cannot be re-superseded or otherwise transitioned by any function in this module, through any path, old or new. The new edge only permits a row currently :approved (not yet :applied) to move directly to :superseded -- :approved was already a non-terminal, already-mutable state before this diff (it already transitions to :applied or :failed via existing functions), so this widening does not make a previously-immutable/final state mutable; it adds one more legal successor to a state that was never immutable. No path exists for an already-:applied review from one promotion to be 're-superseded via a different path' -- supersede_review/3 remains the sole choke point (INV-PRM04-1/INV-RB-8), and :applied was already a legal source status before this diff; this diff changes nothing about that edge.

Cardinality-branching fail-safe direction (task item 5) -- confirmed directly in supersede_matching_review/4: the `[_, _ | _] -> nil` branch (git diff, lib/letflow/definitions.ex) contains zero Repo calls and no side effects of any kind -- it is a bare literal `nil`, reached only after the case's other two branches ([] and [single_review]) are excluded by pattern order. No partial mutation is possible: the single Repo call that can mutate a promotion_reviews row (PromotionReviewStore.supersede_review/3) appears only inside the [single_review] branch, never in the ambiguous branch. This is the exact fail-closed direction the Rework-1 CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR blocker required.

Event-append-after-commit window (task item 6) -- same shape and same already-accepted tradeoff as promote_definition/3's own OQ-1 (lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex moduledoc lines 30-40), confirmed by direct comparison of both call sites: both commit the state-changing transaction first, then call an injected event_appender function outside it. This is not a new gap introduced by REQ-038; it is disclosed explicitly in the design doc (OQ-3) and in this diff's own code comments. Not a violation of any of INV-1..INV-8 (none of the eight invariants governs commit-vs-audit-log ordering directly) -- recorded as a non-blocking observation in issues below since the design doc itself asks REVIEWER to weigh whether rollback's higher security sensitivity changes the calculus, which is REVIEWER's Step 2d call, not SECURITY-REVIEWER's.

Overall: no BLOCKER found on any applicable invariant. PASS.

issues.description: Non-blocking, carried forward for REVIEWER's Step 2d attention per the design doc's own OQ-3: the DEFINITION_VERSION_ROLLED_BACK event is appended after TX1 (the pointer-swap transaction) commits, not inside it -- the same divergence from R-Co's literal single-transaction framing that promote_definition/3 already established and that REVIEWER already accepted for that function. This means there is a real, if narrow, window where the pointer swap is durably visible to any reader before the audit event exists. Not an INV-1..INV-8 violation (no invariant in security-invariants.md governs commit-vs-audit-log sequencing), and the design doc discloses it explicitly (OQ-3) rather than hiding it -- flagged here only because the task briefing specifically asked whether rollback's greater security sensitivity (an admin-gated undo operation) changes the calculus versus routine promotion. SECURITY-REVIEWER's own read: the risk shape is identical to the already-accepted promote_definition/3 precedent (an injected event_appender's transactionality is opaque to the caller by construction, so nesting it inside TX1 would require trusting an arbitrary closure to compose correctly with an open Ecto transaction -- the same reason promotion.ex declined to do so) -- this does not independently rise to BLOCKER under this gate's own invariant list, but REVIEWER should make the explicit call the design doc asks for rather than this being silently inherited as settled.

swap_active_pointer/3's `{1, [activated_row]} = Repo.update_all(...)` bare match (lib/letflow/definitions.ex) required manual reasoning beyond INV-8's grep heuristic to clear -- it is safe only because target_row.id was FOR UPDATE-locked in the same transaction immediately before, mirroring the already-approved activate_draft/2 precedent in the same file. Recorded explicitly per this gate's own instruction not to silently pass a heuristic-only check; no action needed, this is not a FAIL.

result.next_action: Route to REVIEWER (Step 2d) -- pay particular attention to the promotion_review_store.ex allowed_source_statuses widening's REVIEWER sign-off (design §7's own explicit request, distinct from this gate's security-invariant scope) and to OQ-3's event-append-after-commit tradeoff for rollback specifically (issues[0] above).
